title: Corn-tchap (Maize and Bean Stew, Northern Cameroon)
author: Tata Ngome et al. (CIFOR-ICRAF, IRAD, Université de Ngaoundéré)
desc: Whole maize grains simmered about an hour with rock salt and skins washed off, beans cooked about 1½ hours, then both added to a fried onion, tomato and spice base and simmered 5 minutes.
longDesc: A page from the October 2023 recipe book of the ReSI-NoC project (p. 7). The maize is cleaned and cooked in water with sel gemme (natron/kanwa) about an hour, cooled and the skins washed off. Red, black or white (niébé) beans are cooked in salted water about 1 hour 30 and washed. Onion and bell pepper are chopped and the other condiments crushed; the onion is roasted, the crushed condiments added and simmered, seasoned with salt and a stock cube, and the maize and beans stirred in and simmered 5 minutes. Seasoning quantities are not printed.
ingredients: 750 g red, black or white (niébé) beans
Parsley, celery, basil, garlic, ginger — quantities not printed
Salt, chilli, stock cube — quantities not printed
Rock salt (sel gemme, natron/kanwa) — quantity not printed
steps: Clean the maize and cook it in water with the rock salt for about an hour. Cool, then wash off the skins.
Cook the beans in salted water about 1 hour 30. Wash them.
Chop the onion and bell pepper; crush the other condiments.
Roast the onion, add the crushed condiments and simmer.
Season with salt and the stock cube. Add the maize and beans and simmer 5 minutes. Serve.
chefTips: The printed cue for the maize is that the skins loosen and wash off.
The bean time is printed as about 1 hour 30 here and about 20 minutes in the sister recipe Kont-niébé (CMR050).
Seasoning quantities are not printed — season by taste.
commonMistakes: Skipping the rock salt step without noting it is part of the printed method.
healthBenefits: Maize and beans together give carbohydrate, protein and fibre.
culturalNote: The book attributes its recipes to the northern part of Cameroon and names no community, lamidat or town for any recipe.
